sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Notice how the explanation names the reason for each step.

items.prompt: Why restrict the domain of sine before inverting?

steps: Sine repeats, so it is not one-to-one.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Find all solutions of sin θ = 1/2 for 0° ≤ θ < 360°.
Evaluate arcsin(√2/2) in radians, giving the principal value.
Why does cosine on all real numbers not have an inverse function without further restriction?
choices: It is not one-to-one — infinitely many inputs give the same output — so it has no inverse until the domain is restricted to [−π/2, π/2].
It repeats with period π, so the domain is restricted to (−π/2, π/2) to make an inverse possible.
Because its outputs are not all positive.
It is not one-to-one, so the domain is restricted to [0, π] to make an inverse possible.
